decontamination_notes:
Real serialization control-character escaping fix from tafia/quick-xml PR #1001 (https://github.com/tafia/quick-xml/pull/1001, closes #670 and #990), merged 2026-08-15 -- after the training cutoffs of the models evaluated here (e.g. Opus 5, May 2026), so the specific fix is not in their training data (decontaminated: true), with upstream_merged recorded as proof. When writing XML, a literal carriage return in text is silently rewritten to a newline by XML end-of-line normalization, and a newline or tab inside an attribute value is normalized to a space by attribute-value normalization; writing them unescaped corrupts the value on round-trip and, in attribute context, can be used to smuggle/truncate data. The fix makes escape() also escape \r as , adds escape_attribute() which additionally escapes \n as 
 and \t as 	, and switches attribute serialization (src/events/attributes.rs) to use escape_attribute. NOTE ON BASE COMMIT: this PR was rebase-merged, so the merge commit's first parent is an intermediate PR commit that already contains the fix; the true base is the parent of the PR's FIRST commit (6c60dd48), verified to still use the old escape set with no escape_attribute. Sliced at that true base. quick-xml is edition 2021 / rust-version 1.86, so it builds on the :rust image (rustc 1.87); Cargo.toml was trimmed to the single non-optional dependency (memchr) with dev-dependencies/benches/extra test+example targets removed, and memchr is vendored into repo/vendor with repo/.cargo/config.toml for offline (network-off) `cargo test --offline`. The serde-serializer (src/se/*) part of the upstream change is behind the removed `serialize` feature and is not exercised here; hidden tests use only the crate's core public API (quick_xml::escape::escape and the Writer/attribute path), so they compile at the base commit. MIT LICENSE preserved. Coverage floor: 3 fail_to_pass (a \r in text escaped to , and a \n and a \t in an attribute value escaped to 
/	) plus a 2-check regression guard (the five XML predefined entities are still escaped as before; a plain attribute value is written verbatim).
